cases.setup: Bind a public checkout, hashed scope-registry and argument-binding anchors, and public analyzer commands for 'class c: pass; async def func(c: c) -> None: pass' expressed as multiline code and its ordinary-function counterpart. Capture tracked-file content hashes before the probe. Include a second inspection fixture where async registration is already correct.
checks: The probe record contains the actual argv, exit status and diagnostic or exception output for both counterparts, not just a predicted result.
The record identifies ordinary-function registry value shape, whether AsyncFunctionDef is present, the runtime capability guard, and the traced argument-binding scope path at hashed anchors.

For the causal-omission fixture, the emitted scope-review has semantic_role scope-omission-context, artifact_kind code-and-probe-record, language python, scope current-scope-classification, phase pre-edit and state confirmed.
For the already-correct fixture, no confirmed scope-review is emitted and the modifying plan is rejected as not applicable; unavailable causal evidence is recorded UNKNOWN rather than confirmed.
Before/after tracked-file hashes are identical.

cases.setup: Supply the matching confirmed scope-review PortValue and real current registry/test bindings from a public causal-omission fixture. Record the pre-edit ordinary-function registration, capability policy, parent-traversal source, existing diagnostic assertions and validation facts.
checks: The post-edit registry includes the supported async function kind with the same value representation and function-scope semantics as ordinary functions; unavailable AST references remain guarded according to the reviewed policy.
New or cited equivalent public coverage contains a module-level class, identically named annotated async parameter, None return annotation, and the suite's no-diagnostic assertion.
Diff inspection shows parent-traversal source and existing diagnostic expectations unchanged; no Module.parent fallback or global diagnostic suppression is introduced.
The emitted scope-change has semantic_role scope-validation-target, artifact_kind code-and-test-change, language python, scope current-scope-classification, phase post-edit and state unvalidated.
The plan marks public-validation-observed stale and retains scope-validate with validation_for containing this Action ID; no repair-success claim is emitted before validation.
Repeating with a required semantic prerequisite UNKNOWN produces no source edit.

cases.setup: Supply matching unvalidated scope-change and bound current target, ordinary-counterpart, affected-annotation-suite and compatibility Oracles. Exercise one passing fixture, one fixture whose target still crashes, and one with an unresolved required compatibility check. Capture source and expectation hashes before validation.
checks: For each executed Oracle, the validation record contains rendered argv, actual exit status, output, tested identities or scope, and PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN under oracle:<action_id>:<source_oracle_id>.
The passing target and ordinary counterpart finish without Module.parent exceptions or unexpected diagnostics, and the bound affected suite reports passing tests.
Passing acceptance also has evidence-backed ordinary behavior, adjacent diagnostics, runtime compatibility and unchanged downstream traversal checks; a target pass alone is insufficient.
The crashing fixture records FAIL and is not accepted; the unresolved compatibility fixture records UNKNOWN and is not accepted.
The output scope-validation records actual outcomes including failures; async-target-behavior-correct is established only on passing target observations.
Before/after source and expectation hashes are identical, and the report makes no whole-project success claim.

cases.setup: Bind public analyzer commands for two typing.overload declarations followed by their implementation in synchronous and asynchronous forms. Provide current recognition, decorator-resolution, node-family and test anchors. Include negative fixtures with an already async-aware gate and with faulty decorator identity. Capture tracked-file hashes.
checks: The record includes actual argv, exit statuses and diagnostic output for both sequences, plus reviewed decorator identity and current source-node predicate anchors.

For the causal-omission fixture, the synchronous sequence has no unused-redefinition diagnostics while the async sequence fails the intended no-diagnostic assertion, and the inspected predicate excludes the supported async node kind.
The record names supported function AST classes, capability policy and existing public coverage; it does not infer support from async syntax alone.

Only established causal omission emits an overload-review with semantic_role overload-omission-context, artifact_kind code-and-probe-record, language python, scope current-overload-classification, phase pre-edit and state confirmed.
Neither the already async-aware fixture nor the decorator-identity-defect fixture emits confirmed context; unknown evidence remains UNKNOWN and blocks editing.
Tracked-file hashes remain unchanged.

cases.setup: Supply matching confirmed overload-review and current recognition, node-family and test bindings. Capture the original typing-decorator predicate, ordinary redefinition logic, existing expectations and runtime policy.
checks: The edited source-node predicate accepts ordinary and supported async function definitions through the existing overload exemption; an existing equivalent family is reused or a capability-guarded family is introduced.
Diff inspection shows typing decorator identity checks, surrounding ordinary redefinition logic and existing diagnostic expectations unchanged; no global async-warning exemption appears.

New or cited equivalent public regression coverage has two typing.overload-decorated async declarations, an undecorated async implementation of the same name and a no-diagnostic assertion, with runtime handling matching current support policy.

The emitted overload-change has semantic_role overload-validation-target, artifact_kind code-and-test-change, language python, scope current-overload-classification, phase post-edit and state unvalidated.
The plan invalidates public-validation-observed and retains overload-validate with validation_for containing this Action ID.
A run with required semantic prerequisites UNKNOWN makes no source changes and does not claim success.

cases.setup: Supply matching unvalidated overload-change and bind public async/sync overload sequences, an ordinary undecorated unused-name redefinition control, affected-suite commands and compatibility review. Establish the control's baseline diagnostics before edits. Include a passing fixture, a fixture that suppresses the control's diagnostic and a fixture with unresolved runtime compatibility. Capture source and expectation hashes.
checks: Executed Oracles produce records containing rendered argv, actual exit statuses, output, test identities or exact scope, and PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN under their semantic check keys.

In the passing fixture, both overload sequences have zero unused-redefinition warnings, the ordinary control matches its established baseline diagnostic classes and locations, and the affected suite including async and sync cases passes.
Acceptance additionally requires evidence-backed unchanged decorator identity, downstream diagnostic rules and supported-runtime guards.
The diagnostic-suppression fixture records a preservation FAIL and is not accepted even if the async target passes; unresolved runtime compatibility records UNKNOWN and is not accepted.
The emitted overload-validation records failures as well as passes; producing this output alone does not establish async-target-behavior-correct or preservation.
Source and expectation hashes remain unchanged, and the report distinguishes affected-suite results from untested whole-project or cross-project claims.
